brief: A tight crop of a child's scraped knee with a half-peeled adhesive plaster, built the way birch bark is built. Chalky white and pale bone washes are laid in thin papery sheets with lifted, curling edges. Short horizontal charcoal dashes become the grazes, pores and creases. Soft graphite carries the rounded form, and touches of raw sienna and pink madder sit in the raw skin. The plaster's fabric weave and the curling gauze edge are drawn in hard pencil. The light is cool and overcast, and the palette stays almost monochrome. The image is intimate and slightly clinical.

A grandfather flipping burgers at a backyard grill, seen as a single frame of a home movie. The image is warm, faded and colour-shifted toward amber and cyan-green shadows. Heavy spray grain covers everything, and the corners darken in a soft vignette. An orange light leak bleeds from the right edge. His hands, the apron stains, the spatula and the meat fat flare are rendered with startling precision but softened by slight motion blur. Smoke drifts in loose, smudged washes. The mood is nostalgic, tender and flickering.

A pawnshop sign in daylight, its neon tubes switched off and dusty behind smeared plate glass. The bent glass tubing is the subject. It is drawn in fine pen with crisp paired highlight lines showing the tube walls, pale coral and mint phosphor tints inside, and blackened electrode caps with wire clips. The window glass layers faint reflections of the street, parked cars and sky over the scene in thin grey washes. Dead flies and dust collect on the sill. The light is flat and greyish, and the mood is quiet and forensic.

A worn tennis ball resting in dewy morning lawn, filling most of the frame. It is built entirely from soft fibrous mass: misted spray for the underlying chartreuse and dirty optic-yellow body, then thousands of tiny curled pencil fibres standing proud of the surface. A halo of loose fuzz catches the low sunlight along the rim. The white seam is felted and matted, and grass blades press dents into the nap. Dew beads sit on the fibres with sharp refractions. There is no hard outline anywhere except the water droplets. The image is tactile, warm and soft.

From inside a parked pickup, a towering wall of dust fills the windshield. It is a dense spray gradient that runs from ochre to rust to bruised umber and swallows the horizon. Against that soft wall the foreground stays brutally sharp. A cracked vinyl dashboard, a dangling rosary, a coffee cup lid and grit settling along the wiper are all drawn in hard fine pen with tight marker shading. The contrast between the fuzzy airborne mass and the exact plastic textures carries the piece. The light is dim and amber, as if the sun has been strained through cloth.

A worm's-eye view of a coiled rubber garden hose hanging from a wall bracket. The loops sweep in whiplash Art Nouveau curves and tendrils of spilled water drip from the brass nozzle. Fine pen line holds every curve, and the hose is shaded in layered markers of verdigris and bottle green with hard enamel highlights. A dark hairline shadow sits under each coil. Behind it, a weathered stone wall in pale limestone wash stays muted so the organic metalwork rhythm dominates. The piece feels ornamental and civic, an ordinary object promoted to wrought-iron grandeur.

A single unbroken ribbon of red apple peel hangs in the air above a scarred wooden cutting board. It twists back on itself in two orbiting lobes, like a strange attractor traced through space. The peel is rendered in fine continuous pen with dense coloured-pencil layering, in crimson streaked with chartreuse and flecked with lenticels, and its moist white underside catches light. The paring knife and the naked apple sit sharp below, with sticky juice beads in marker. Dark slate surrounds everything. The feeling is mathematical yet edible, chaos made orderly by a steady hand.

A hyperreal side profile of a young man with close-cropped curls, drawn as though carved from layered sardonyx. Pale shell-white highlights rise from a deep caramel-brown toned ground. Raking light from one side makes the relief read physically, from the ridge of the brow and the curve of the ear to the soft shadow under the jaw. The figure is built in white and cream pencil over dark wash, with fine hatching for the hair. A thin oval border frames him. The real skin texture of pores, stubble and a tiny scar keeps the image alive rather than ornamental.

A veiled chameleon gripping a flowering pomegranate twig. Its scaled skin is rendered with hyperreal precision but coloured in the mordant-dyed palette of Indian chintz: madder red, indigo, saffron, lac purple and leaf green layered as flat transparent watercolour within confident black pen outlines. Every bead-like scale is outlined like a resist line, then flooded with dye. The ground is warm unbleached cotton, glazed so it has a faint polished sheen. The composition is a tall vertical with the curling tail as a strong spiral. The feel is luxurious, exotic and minutely crafted.

The frontage of a corner laundromat in flat noon light, painted with the cool total clarity of seventies Photorealism. Rows of chrome front-loaders inside overlap with the plate-glass reflections of the street: a parked sedan, a bus-stop sign, a doubled awning. Everything is equally in focus. It is drawn with ruled fine pen and built up in smooth unmodulated marker in chrome grey, mint, tangerine and sky blue. There is no figure and no story, only layered surfaces and mirrored geometry. The feeling is deadpan, gleaming and slightly uncanny.

A close overhead crop of a woman's hand gripping a dented steel tumbler of milky chai, with fresh henna drying across the palm and fingers. The paste lines are raised and glossy, rendered with marker and fine pen so they stand above the skin, and some flakes have dropped to reveal the bright orange stain beneath. The skin is built in warm watercolour glazes of sienna and rose, with pores and knuckle creases drawn in pencil. The steel reflects distorted fragments of the hand and cooled lattices of lace. The atmosphere is intimate and festive, hours before a wedding.

A sleeping tabby cat, curled nose-to-tail into the compact coiled pose of Scythian gold animal plaques, lies on deep black velvet. Every hair is real, but the fur stripes swirl into stylised spirals and comma shapes. The rendering uses layered watercolour and marker in raw sienna, Naples yellow and burnished ochre, with sharp white-gold highlights on the haunch, ear and paw pads. Fine pen picks out whiskers and claws. Strong top light gives the cat the sheen of hammered metal. The mood is regal and dormant, a treasure that happens to breathe.

A heavy bunch of green grapes lying on wet pebbles. Each berry carries a matte frosted bloom that makes it look like tumbled sea glass, softly translucent with light glowing through from behind. The rendering uses many thin watercolour glazes of seafoam, celadon and pale aquamarine, with chalky white pencil rubbed over for the bloom. Only a few spots, where a thumb has polished the berry, show crisp glassy highlights. Tiny water droplets bead on the stems. The mood is cool, quiet and shoreline-soft.

A hyperreal portrait of an old surfer, cropped from brow to chin and filling the frame. His skin is treated like weathered driftwood. Wrinkles run in long flowing graphite hatching that follows the contours the way wood grain follows a branch. The palette is silver-grey, bone and faded salt-white, with only a hint of sunburnt pink at the nose and lips. Salt crystals cling to his stubble, picked out in white against soft grey shading. The light is flat sea-haze. The mood is stoic and eroded, a face shaped by wind and tide.

A hyperreal stack of unglazed clay roof tiles on a building-site pallet, seen from a low diagonal so the curved lips recede in a long repeating rhythm. Built from layered watercolour washes of burnt sienna, raw umber and Venetian red, scumbled over with dry chalky charcoal-like mass so the surface reads as porous, powdery fired clay. Each tile has crisp pencil-sharp chips, a pale efflorescence bloom and fine hairline cracks. Flat overcast light keeps the shadows soft and earthy. The palette never leaves the fired-earth family. The mood is dry and dusty, the warmth of brick that has just come out of the kiln.

The interior of a timber workshop at late afternoon. Sharp crepuscular rays slant through gaps in plank walls and cut solid beams through hanging sawdust. The scene is built in dense charcoal-like mass and smudged darks, with the beams lifted out in white and pale amber pencil and streaked with drifting motes. Inside one shaft, a sawhorse holds a half-cut board. Its fresh pine end grain, the steel saw teeth and the curled shavings are rendered with razor clarity. Everything outside the light falls into velvety murk. The atmosphere is warm, laborious and hushed.

A diagonal procession of ghost crabs crossing dark wet sand, rendered hyperreally. Their carapaces, stalked eyes and jointed legs repeat like embroidered figures on a Paracas mantle. The palette is cochineal red, gold ochre, deep olive and indigo against a near-black ground. Build every surface with dense, directional coloured-pencil hatching that reads like stitch work, packed tight and following each form's curvature. Glints of wet shell come from small burnished highlights. The crabs vary subtly in pose and colour so the pattern breathes. The sand shows faint tracks between them. It feels ancient, rhythmic and quietly uncanny.

A tight hyperreal crop where the seat tube of a racing bicycle meets its top tube. Its carbon-fibre weave is rendered in disciplined pencil basketweave crosshatching, with each tow catching light differently so the checker pattern seems to shift. A clear lacquer shell carries a curving window-reflection highlight. A neon chartreuse decal edge is cut crisp in marker, and a bead of sweat and a gritty road smear sit nearby. The palette is gunmetal, graphite and electric yellow on a pale studio grey. The mood is technical, fast and engineered.

A hyperreal overhead view of a well-used wooden palette. Fresh oil paint has been squeezed out in fat, ridged coils and rosettes, like buttercream piping from a star nozzle. There are blobs of titanium white, cadmium red, cerulean and Naples yellow. Each extruded ridge is modelled with layered marker and soft pencil, given glossy specular crests and creamy shadows in the grooves. Dried paint crusts and a crimped aluminium tube with its cap off sit at the edges. The light is soft north-window daylight. The mood is luscious, edible and craft-proud.

Two hyperreal brown quail nestle in dry millet stalks on a warm, tea-stained silk-toned ground. Every feather is outlined in hair-fine, unwavering ink lines, then built up through dozens of transparent mineral washes in burnt sienna, ochre and pale azurite. The breast scallops, speckled throats and glossy black eyes are rendered with meticulous patience. Millet heads are dotted grain by grain in malachite and straw. The composition is asymmetrical, with deliberate empty silk in the upper left. The edges are precise and calm, and the mood is courtly, patient and serene.
